Chloe — thanks for the ping. Short answers first: 1) Classification: if EdgeTransit performs network transit only (no TLS termination and no persistent logging beyond ephemeral flow records) we treat them as a carrier-level transit partner rather than a subprocessor; however, if they terminate TLS or have any ability to inspect application-layer traffic, they must be listed as a subprocessor and we should capture A&A evidence.

2) Minimum controls to request from Greenleaf/EdgeTransit if they want an attestation:
- Explicit statement whether EdgeTransit will terminate TLS or act as a proxy (yes/no).
- If TLS is terminated: provide cert management and HSM/KMS details.
- Network log retention window (we recommend <= 30 days unless justified).
- Whether any packet capture (pcap) or deep packet inspection will be stored; if so, where and for how long.
- Access control and admin ACLs for EdgeTransit ops staff (MFA, RBAC).
- Encryption in transit (TLS1.2+ required) and at-rest for any persisted captures.

3) Evidence we can share quickly: we can provide the current subprocessor roster (redwood_subprocessor_roster_may2028.xlsx) and a one-page statement describing our network flow model and where TLS is terminated (we do TLS at the load balancer and do not terminate inside the model servers). For the temporary arrangement, if EdgeTransit will not terminate TLS and only provides scalar transit, I can sign off on classification as transit partner. If they will terminate TLS, we need their SOC2/ISO27001 docs and a short control matrix.

Ill draft a short control checklist (attached) you can send to Tim. Naomi — please weigh in on retention and legal language for a temporary passthrough clause.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Subprocessor passthrough for EdgeTransit - quick info request

Hi Tim — thanks for the patience. We reviewed this internally with Security and Privacy. Summary below and attached materials for your audit folder.

Short summary:
- Classification: At present EdgeTransit will be treated as a temporary subprocessor if they will terminate TLS or perform application-layer routing. If EdgeTransit is strictly providing layer-3/4 transit with no TLS termination and no packet capture storage, we classify them as a carrier-level transit partner (not a subprocessor).
- Redwood network model: TLS is terminated at our edge load balancers (configured with TLS1.3), and model servers only receive decrypted traffic inside our private network when TLS is intentionally proxied. For the planned transit scenario, our preference is that EdgeTransit does not terminate TLS.
- Retention and logging: Redwood retains flow-level metadata for 14 days by default. We do not persist application payloads. If EdgeTransit stores network captures, we require retention <= 30 days and encryption-at-rest with documented ACLs.

What we attached:
- redwood_subprocessor_roster_may2028.xlsx (current roster; includes services that may see logs)
- edgetransit_temp_controls.pdf (checklist wed like EdgeTransit to complete; also lists required evidence if they terminate TLS)

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether EdgeTransit will perform TLS termination?
2) If yes, please have EdgeTransit return the completed checklist and their SOC2/ISO attestation documents. If no, confirm in writing (email is fine) that they will not perform TLS termination and will not retain application payloads beyond transient buffering.

If it helps, Naomi is copied and can draft the temporary passthrough clause language for your DPA addendum once we know classification. We can also offer a short joint call with EdgeTransit if thats easier.

Best,
Chloe Martin
